doc.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

chapter: Riverwalk radio show and Porgy and Bess
title: Working with a guest vocalist on the show
summary: After an audio clip of a guest singer, Cullum says the band recreated a small-ensemble setting to make him comfortable.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I brought a little piece from one of your shows if I could make it happen here. Oh that’s not it, hold on. I wanted to get it up, I will in a second here, because you had a guest, one of our favorite people, and I did want to try to get it up here. It’s a guessing game but, one of Hamilton’s favorite people.
You remember that show? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-
It’s interesting to hear this arrangement with the smaller ensemble.
Of course we were trying to make it sound, you know, we were trying to make it sound something like it. That’s our rhythm section.
What was Joe like to work with on that show?

Well he was a professional you know. We got up there and we did that and we talked it through ahead of time and I think it was pretty straight forward to go at it. He got in there and got out of there, to do the show.
Is it different working with vocalists than it is with instrumentalists?
Well vocalists have special requirements sometimes. They have special needs, musical needs I mean. I don’t mean —
No, I know what you mean.

So in this case we had, that’s not our normal band deal and we had recreated this whole thing to make him at home and him comfortable and give him the kind of sound that would make him comfortable, and what he expected and what would feel good to him and would sound natural to him.
